title: Contractible fibers turn a right fibration into a trivial Kan fibration
statement: Use simplicial sets, horns, Kan complexes and weak contractibility as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and trivial Kan fibrations in the boundary-lifting sense of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], including dimension zero. Let $q:E\to S$ be a simplicial map, with no quasicategory assumption on $S$. Suppose $q$ has the right lifting property against every horn inclusion $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ with $n\geq1$ and $0<i\leq n$ (so $q$ is a right fibration). Suppose for every vertex $s\in S_0$ the degreewise fiber $E_s=\{s\}\times_SE$ is a weakly contractible Kan complex. Then $q$ is a trivial Kan fibration.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.2.14 (01NU), implication (3) to (1). The right-fibration convention is Definition 4.2.1.1, right-handed variant; weak contractibility has the project convention. This is a Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag. Online source read; archival copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: The dimension-zero condition of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration] is surjectivity on vertices. For $s\in S_0$, weak contractibility in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] makes the realization of $E_s$ nonempty, since its set of path components maps bijectively to that of a point. A nonempty realization has a representing simplex; restricting that simplex to a vertex gives a vertex of $E_s$. Thus $s$ has a lift. If $S$ is empty this condition is vacuous.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.2.15, dimension-zero argument, with right/left interchanged.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq1$ and a lifting square $a:\partial\Delta^n\to E$, $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$. Put $X=\Delta^n\times_S E$ and $p:X\to\Delta^n$. For a right-horn square against $p$, compose its top map with $X\to E$, lift against $q$, and pair this lift with the specified bottom map to $\Delta^n$; the resulting pair lands in the pullback. Thus $p$ is a right fibration. The given boundary map is now $a':\partial\Delta^n\to X$ over the boundary inclusion. Moreover $X$ is a quasicategory: an inner horn into $X$ projects to an inner horn in $\Delta^n$; the latter fills because a simplex of $\Delta^n$ is a weakly increasing list of vertices, and the vertices of an inner horn are weakly increasing (for a two-dimensional inner horn this follows from its two consecutive edges; in higher dimensions every edge is present). Fill the resulting square against $p$. The fiber $X_0$ over vertex $0$ is exactly $E_{\sigma(0)}$ and is weakly contractible Kan by hypothesis. This argument uses only the degreewise pullback and horn definitions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and assumes nothing about $S$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.2.15, pullback reduction to a standard simplex and the inner-horn check; right-handed dual.

proof.text: Let $B=\partial\Delta^n$ and let $c:\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\to\Delta^n$ be induced by the monotone map $c(0,j)=0$, $c(1,j)=j$. The inclusion $\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ is the right-horn inclusion $\Lambda_1^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product] to it and to the degreewise injective map $\varnothing\hookrightarrow B$: its pushout-product is $j:\{1\}\times B\hookrightarrow\Delta^1\times B$, so $j$ is right anodyne. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-exponentiation] to $p$ and $j$. By the internal-functor definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the pair consisting of $c|_{\Delta^1\times B}$ and $a'$ is a vertex of the target of the resulting exponential restriction map. The dimension-zero surjectivity clause of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration] gives a source vertex. This is exactly a map $h':\Delta^1\times B\to X$ with $ph'=c|_{\Delta^1\times B}$ and $h'|_{\{1\}\times B}=a'$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.2.15, boundary homotopy lift, right-handed dual; Kerodon Propositions 4.2.5.3 (0153) and 4.2.5.4 (0154).

proof.text: The restriction $h'|_{\{0\}\times B}$ lands in $X_0$. The map $X_0\to\Delta^0$ is a Kan fibration: a lifting square against a horn is just a horn map into $X_0$, which extends since $X_0$ is Kan. This map is a weak homotopy equivalence by the weak-contractibility hypothesis. Apply the weak-equivalence-to-trivial-fibration implication of [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion] to $X_0\to\Delta^0$. Its boundary-lifting conclusion extends the restriction to $v:\Delta^n\to X_0$. Glue $v$ and $h'$ along their identical restrictions on $\{0\}\times B$, degree by degree. This gives a map $g_0:W_0=(\Delta^1\times B)\cup(\{0\}\times\Delta^n)\to X$ lying over $c$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.2.15 (01A7), contractible-fiber extension over the initial end of the prism, right-handed version; Proposition 3.3.7.6 (00ZP), (3) implies (1), applied only to the Kan fibration X_0 to a point.

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-infinity-right-prism-boundary] in dimension $n$. Here is the explicit reindexing that puts its filtration at endpoint $0$. For a monotone $\alpha:[r]\to[s]$ define $\alpha^{\mathrm{rev}}(j)=s-\alpha(r-j)$, and for a simplicial set $T$ define $T^{\mathrm{rev}}_r=T_r$ with operator $T(\alpha^{\mathrm{rev}})$. This is an involutive reindexing functor: $(\alpha\beta)^{\mathrm{rev}}=\alpha^{\mathrm{rev}}\beta^{\mathrm{rev}}$, so it preserves degreewise products, unions and pushouts. Identify $(\Delta^a)^{\mathrm{rev}}$ with $\Delta^a$ by sending a degree-$r$ list $u$ to the list $j\mapsto a-u(r-j)$. On the prism this sends the cited endpoint-$1$ filtration $X_k$ to a filtration $W_k$ beginning with the $W_0$ of step 4, ending at $W_{n+1}=\Delta^1\times\Delta^n$, and satisfying $W_{k+1}=W_k\cup\operatorname{im}(\theta_k)$. The reversed cell $\sigma_k$ has ordered vertices $(0,0),\ldots,(0,n-k),(1,n-k),\ldots,(1,n)$. Reversing the $n+2$ domain vertices sends the omitted face $k+1$ to $n-k$. Thus each $W_k\hookrightarrow W_{k+1}$ is the pushout of $\Lambda_{n-k}^{n+1}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{n+1}$ along this cell; the map $\theta_k$ is degreewise injective since its displayed vertices are distinct. This also proves $\theta_k^{-1}(W_k)=\Lambda_{n-k}^{n+1}$, since the pushout is computed degreewise and both attaching maps are injective. For $k=0,\ldots,n-1$, inductively compose $g_k$ with the horn attaching map and use the bottom map $c\theta_k$. Since $1\leq n-k\leq n$, the right-fibration property of $p$ supplies a filler. The pushout glues it with $g_k$ to $g_{k+1}$ over $c$. This constructs $g_n$. When $n=1$, the first cell has vertices $(0,0),(0,1),(1,1)$ and attaches along $\Lambda_1^2$.

source.place: Kerodon Lemma 4.4.2.15 (01A7), right-handed dual of the finite prism induction; Lemma 3.1.2.12 (00TH), dual filtration with forward stage k and horn n-k.

proof.text: The final pushout obtained in step 5 from [lem-coef-infinity-right-prism-boundary] attaches $\theta_n$ with vertices $(0,0),(1,0),(1,1),\ldots,(1,n)$ along $\Lambda_0^{n+1}$. Its initial edge lies in $\Delta^1\times\partial\Delta^n$, because $n\geq1$ puts vertex $0$ in that boundary, and its projection under $c$ is constant at $0$. Consequently its image $e:x\to y$ under $g_n$ is an edge of the Kan fiber $X_0$. We check explicitly that its image in $X$ is an equivalence in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fill in $X_0$ the horn $\Lambda_0^2$ whose edges $01$ and $02$ are $e$ and $\mathrm{id}_x$. Write $\tau$ for the filler and $g:y\to x$ for its edge $12$, so $\tau$ witnesses $ge=\mathrm{id}_x$. Next fill $\Lambda_0^3$ with faces $d_1=s_0e$, $d_2=s_1e$ and $d_3=\tau$; their shared edges agree, with vertices $(x,y,x,y)$. Its face $d_0$ has edges $01=g$, $12=e$, $02=\mathrm{id}_y$ and witnesses $eg=\mathrm{id}_y$. Applying the inclusion $X_0\to X$ preserves both triangles and identity edges. The quasicategory $X$ from step 2 therefore satisfies the initial-edge hypothesis of [lem-cbc-equivalence-outer-horn-filling] with $m=n+1\geq2$. That node gives an absolute filler $w:\Delta^{n+1}\to X$ for the prescribed horn. Every vertex lies in this horn, so $pw$ and $c\theta_n$ agree on vertices; maps from $\Delta^{n+1}$ to $\Delta^n$ are determined by their monotone vertex lists. Thus $pw=c\theta_n$. The final pushout glues $w$ with $g_n$ to $h:\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\to X$ over $c$, retaining $h'$ on the boundary cylinder. For $n=1$, faces $1$ and $2$ of this last cell are the previously attached diagonal and the edge over vertex $0$; face $0$, the time-one edge, is absent. The attaching domain is $\Lambda_0^2$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.2.15, final exceptional horn, right-handed dual; Theorem 4.4.2.6 (019F), initial-edge version.

proof.text: Restrict $h$ to $\{1\}\times\Delta^n$ and project $X\to E$. Since $c(1,j)=j$, its composite with $q$ is exactly $\sigma$. Since $h$ agrees with $h'$ on $\Delta^1\times\partial\Delta^n$, its boundary is exactly $a$. This solves the arbitrary positive-dimensional boundary square. Together with step 1 it is precisely the definition of trivial Kan fibration in [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration].

source.place: Proposition 4.4.2.14 (01NU), (3) implies (1), after its cited Lemma 4.4.2.15.
